text:
maria: Heads-up — we saw a noticeable cost spike in eu-west overnight, mostly from preemptible instance churn. Spot reclaim rate up ~2.3x compared to last week. Noticed higher retry tail for batch jobs.

ajay: I saw that too. Most of the churn aligns with the 02:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window in that region. Could be competing workloads from partner accounts.

sophie: Interactive latency SLOs were fine, so the noise seems concentrated in our low-priority batch tier. Batch queue backlog increased ~18% which pushed some retries into peak hours.

tim: Proposal: enable a targeted off-peak burst scheduling policy + segmentation of GPU pools. Keep interactive on dedicated/durable capacity; move elastic batch bursts to preemptible-only pools in secondary regions.

maria: Agreed conceptually. Want to ensure we have graceful interruption handling for the burst pool: checkpointing, soft preemption notices, and faster rescheduling to alternate region.

ajay: We can use the provider's 30s advance-notice webhook to trigger KV checkpoints and short-lived model shard flush. Also propose a "soft-preempt" drain that gives jobs a 60s window to flush.

sophie: Need to validate that our user-facing retry policy won't amplify cost by spinning up new instances too eagerly. Maybe add exponential backoff + max-retries per job during off-peak bursts.

tim: Sketch of queue config prototype (will iterate):
```
queues:
  interactive:
    preemptible: false
    reserved_gpus: 0.3
    sla_class: p0
  batch_elastic:
    preemptible: true
    max_burst_gpus: 120
    offpeak_window: "00:00-07:00 UTC"
    soft_preempt_seconds: 60
    reschedule_policy: "prefer-secondary-region"
```

maria: Also add a cost-target metric for the burst pool (cost-per-token or cost-per-second) and auto-scale down when cost > target for 15m. We want automation to cap runaway spend.

ajay: Will prototype autoscale + cost gating. One wrinkle: networking and NVLink pinned workloads won't migrate easily between regions. We'll need a fallback to local low-priority nodes rather than cross-region if model is too large.

sophie: Good call. For very large models mark them "affinity: local-only" in the job manifest. For smaller ones allow region-fallback. We'll update job schema.

infra-bot: deploy started: patch 'burst-scheduler-v0.1' -> infra-cluster-dev (CI)

maria: Action items:
- ajay: prototype scheduler patch and soft-preempt hook (ETA EOD+2).
- sophie: audit SLOs & tweak retry/backoff defaults for batch_elastic (ETA EOD+3).
- tim: draft runbook for interruption handling + cost-gating thresholds (ETA EOD+4).
- maria: schedule a quick sync w/ capacity planning to review region quotas and reserved fallback (ETA tomorrow).

maria: If nobody objects I'd like to run a small canary next off-peak window and measure cost delta + success rate. :thumbsup:

ajay: +1. I'll post the canary results in #eng-infra with metrics (reclaim rate, avg reschedule latency, cost-per-burst).

sophie: :rocket:

tim: :hourglass_flowing_sand: will add a known-issues section about NVLink/huge-model affinity to the runbook.

maria: Thanks team, keeping this tight will help reduce unit-cost variability.
